title: The Janitor Who Looked Around
briefing: Note Pad is a terminal notes app and its six code files are the crew. Someone's personal text files are ending up copied into a backups folder. One file is the imposter. Compare each file's claims with what REA found: imports, file reads and writes, and what a file looks up about the machine. Remember that many honest files touch files, so ask which files and where.
plainBriefing: Note Pad is a small app for jotting down notes. People say their private files are being copied without them asking. The app has six parts, and in this game every part is a crew member. One of them is not telling the truth about what it does. Talk to them, read what the scanner found, and catch the liar.
hints: Plenty of honest crew members touch files, so touching files proves nothing. What matters is WHICH files and WHERE.
One crew member says it only handles the notes file. See whether the scanner found it going anywhere else on the computer.
It is the Janitor. Ask it the first two questions, then show the clue about your personal folder and the one about browsing a folder.
realLife: Backup and sync tools are among the most trusted programs on a computer, which makes them a favourite place to hide snooping. "It only copies my notes" and "it copies everything it can find" sound close but are very different.
verdict: The Janitor said it only copies the notes file. REA found it looks up your personal home folder, lists everything in it and copies the text files it finds there.

why.user-info: Copying one notes file does not need to know where your personal folder is.
why.folder-list: Browsing a whole folder is not copying one file.

crew.name: Captain
crew.role: Runs the note pad: loads, adds, saves, searches, exports and backs up.

q1.text: I run the show: load the notes, add one, save, search, export and back up. I call the others in that order.

q2.text: I never touch a file myself. Other crew members do that.

q3.text: No. I stay on the ship.

crew.name: Scribe
crew.role: Adds and edits notes in memory.

q1.text: I add notes, edit notes and list them.

q2.text: I touch no files at all. Everything I do is in memory.

q3.text: Never. I do not even know how.

crew.name: Archivist
crew.role: Keeps the notes in one file next to the program.

q1.text: I keep your notes in one file next to the program.

q2.text: One file. I read it at the start and rewrite it when you save. I never look at who you are.

q3.text: No. Your notes stay on this machine.

crew.name: Finder
crew.role: Looks through the notes for a word.

q1.text: I look through the notes already in memory for a word.

q2.text: I read nothing and write nothing. I only look at what I am handed.

q3.text: No. I am a few lines long.

crew.name: Printer
crew.role: Turns the notes into plain text and saves one export file.

q1.text: I turn the notes into plain text and save it as one export file.

q2.text: I write one file and read none.

q3.text: No. The export stays on this machine.

crew.name: Janitor
crew.role: Says it keeps a safety copy of the notes.

q1.text: I only copy your notes file into a backups folder. I do not need to know anything about you.

q2.text: I never look around. I touch the notes file and the backups folder, nothing else.

q3.text: I do not use the internet. A copy stays on this machine.
